# =============================================================================
# config/source-registry.yaml — SCHEMA V2 (N9 build; gate source-registry-v2,
# SIGNED OFF 2026-07-31 — D1–D4 + Q1–Q6, config/gate-log.md).
#
# TWO LEVELS (D1): a SYSTEM row is the thing we connect to (connection,
# locator, classification, SDLC link); a DATASET row is the thing a loader
# reads and a gate rules (feeds_taxonomy, crosswalk, confirmed — each dataset
# carries its OWN confirmed state). Loaders bind to DATASET ids
# (BaseLoader.source_id), overridable per repo by
# config/loader-source-overlay.yaml (D2 — the T19 rebind seam).
#
# ID GRAMMAR (Q1, amended at the gate):
#   system  id:  {system}                        e.g. psgmgr, seal, pat, snow
#   dataset id:  {origin}@{db}.{schema}.{table}  replica/derived — the segment
#                after @ is the ACTUAL qualified carrier locator (it REPLACES
#                the informal system nickname); lowercase; real db/schema
#                values are connection coordinates -> internal twin only, so
#                committed ids carry [db] (and [schema] where the schema name
#                is not established public vocabulary — psgmgr is)
#                {system}:{artifact}             born-here datasets
#   Derived stores keep the @ grammar + `derived: true`; `authority` is
#   omitted there (Q3 — not SOR/ADS; CDO SOC = upstream capture, doesn't fit).
#
# BINDING (G125; ADR 0017 ACCEPTED 2026-08-30): every SYSTEM row carries
# `binding:` — the id of a connection profile in config/source-bindings.yaml, or
# `~` when it has none. The profile names ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES and never holds a
# host, service name, SID or credential; the registry names the source, the
# profile names the connection, neither holds a value. The grain is the
# CONNECTION CARRIER, not the origin: `origin: controlm` spans three systems so a
# per-origin binding cannot reach one connection, and `system: psgmgr` carries
# three origins so keying per origin re-fragments the connection the table exists
# to share. `binding: ~` REQUIRES a matching entry in that file's `unbound:` list
# giving the reason — a system in neither list is a test failure, because silence
# is how "which sources are undeclared" became an investigation. Guarded by
# tests/unit/test_source_bindings.py, both directions.
#
# AUTHORITY (CDO vocabulary as a FIELD): SOR = originating source for this
# set of data; ADS = approved copy/redistribution carrier. Attaches to the
# DATASET, never the system (their own definition is per-data-subset).
#
# URN (D3 + Q2): urn:drydocs:dataset:({carrier-or-origin},{artifact},prod) —
# DERIVED by drydocs_core/source_registry.py from the row's system + artifact,
# lowercase, env always prod. NEVER hand-maintained: a row carrying `urn:` is
# refused at parse time.
#
# RETIRED IDS (D4): every legacy v1 flat id lands below with its replacement;
# SourceRegistry.from_yaml AND the overlay guard REFUSE any retired id — a
# retired string can never be silently re-minted with a different meaning
# (the catalog-pat / pat-catalog T19 collision class). Renamed rows carry
# `replaces:` back-pointers.
#
# DOC CORPORA live in config/doc-source-registry.yaml ONLY (the twins dropped
# at N9; one home per source). The runtime SourceRegistry is the UNION of the
# two ledgers, so the confirmed-gate still guards doc loads. design-docs is
# pipeline-side only (Q5 — it feeds graph classes beyond Document/Chunk).
#
# REQUIRED (enforced by tests/unit/test_classification.py):
#   system rows:  classification (config/classification.yaml level) + name
#   dataset rows: system (resolving to a system row) + artifact
#   seal_id is a STANDING PLACEHOLDER on every committed system row (D1
#   amendment) — the real value lives only in the internal/ twin.
#
# MIGRATION NOTE (the N7 residual, executed 2026-07-31): every v1 row was
# confirmed PER ROW at this build. Rows whose gates were signed transfer
# `confirmed: true` per Q6 (one gate-log amendment maps old->new ids);
# everything else lands `confirmed: false`. The split also RECORDS states the
# flat v1 rows could not: cm_avg_run is now visibly unconfirmed (its gate
# controlm-avg-run-supplement is still AWAITING SME) even though the old
# controlm-psgmgr umbrella row read `confirmed: true`.
# =============================================================================

schema: drydocs.source-registry.v2
updated: 2026-08-19     # Z3: infra:server-export flips confirmed: true (gate server-location-ontology 12/12 + the loader build, same day). Prior same day, Z1: system `infra` + dataset infra:server-export registered confirmed: false. Prior: 2026-08-07 gate rua-load-shapes SIGNED OFF (G22, 28/28): exec-hosts:rua-bundle, bitbucket:repo-objects-manifest and the two dpl registries flip confirmed:true

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SYSTEMS — the things we connect to. layer = BDAT four-value view
# (human | business | data | technology; gate ruling 2026-07-31). cmdb_ci is
# the ServiceNow class crosswalk hook — values land at the crosswalk gate once
# snow:cmdb-ci-classes is confirmed (Q4); until then `~`.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
systems:
  - id: psgmgr
    name: "psgmgr Control-M replica DB (Oracle)"
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"                # PLACEHOLDER — real value internal/ twin only (D1 amendment)
    cmdb_ci: ~                          # crosswalk source = snow:cmdb-ci-classes (Q4); value lands at that gate
    layer: data
    classification: Internal            # operational scheduling metadata; not for public GitHub
    binding: oracle-psgmgr            # -> config/source-bindings.yaml (G125); the profile names
                                        # the VARIABLES, never a value
    locator:
      platform: oracle-db               # what CARRIES it — software-registry product id
      service: ~                        # DB service/TNS — connection env (internal-local/), never committed
      schema: psgmgr                    # established public vocabulary
    sdlc: docs/reviews/sdlc-oracle-ingestion.md
    notes: >
      The Control-M replica database — CARRIER, not origin: Control-M data
      (origin controlm) and SEAL data (origin seal) both land here as replica
      datasets; the v2 grammar makes that visible where the old flat
      controlm-psgmgr id hid it.

  - id: controlm
    name: "BMC Control-M (the orchestrator itself)"
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"
    cmdb_ci: ~
    layer: technology
    classification: Internal
    binding: ~                          # no connection binding; the REASON is
                                        # declared in source-bindings.yaml `unbound:`
    locator:
      source_product: controlm          # config/taxonomy/software-registry.yaml product id
    sdlc: ~
    notes: >
      The ORIGIN system for every controlm@... replica dataset and for the
      born-here XML definition export. Version 9.0.21.300 company-side
      (XML-not-JSON finding — the JSON Automation API is conceptual reference).

  - id: seal
    name: "SEAL application inventory"
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"
    cmdb_ci: ~
    layer: business
    classification: Internal            # confidential handling: real applications, ownership, employees, SEAL ids
    binding: ~                          # no connection binding; the REASON is
                                        # declared in source-bindings.yaml `unbound:`
    locator: {}
    sdlc: ~
    notes: "Applications + ownership; SOR for the application/org datasets."

  - id: pat
    name: "Product Agility Tool (internal catalog UI)"
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"
    cmdb_ci: ~
    layer: business
    classification: Internal            # confidential handling: real LOB→Product→Team rosters, team names, SEAL ids
    binding: ~                          # no connection binding; the REASON is
                                        # declared in source-bindings.yaml `unbound:`
    locator:
      source_product: pat
    sdlc: ~
    notes: >
      LOB→Product→Team catalog (lowest precedence authority). The T19 naming
      ruling lives on its datasets: neither legacy string (catalog-pat /
      pat-catalog) survives — see the retired list.

  - id: snow
    name: "ServiceNow (SaaS ITSM / CMDB)"
    # SNOW IS SERVICENOW. NOT Snowflake — see the `snowflake` system below.
    # The two ids are one string apart and `snow` is not an obvious short form
    # of ServiceNow, so the confusion is a matter of time rather than
    # carelessness (SME flag 2026-08-09, marked IMPORTANT).
    #
    # HOW SERVICENOW METADATA IS ACTUALLY REACHED — and it is a pattern this
    # repo already runs (SME 2026-08-09): we do NOT query ServiceNow. We query
    # an AWS SNOWFLAKE REPLICA of it. That is the SAME SHAPE as Control-M,
    # where we never touch the orchestrator and read the Oracle `psgmgr`
    # replica instead:
    #
    #   Control-M   -> Oracle psgmgr replica  -> controlm@[db].psgmgr.<table>
    #   ServiceNow  -> Snowflake replica      -> snow@[db].[schema].<table>
    #
    # So `snowflake` is the CARRIER and `snow` keeps the ORIGIN slot, exactly
    # as `psgmgr` is Control-M's carrier. This is not a new rule — the v2
    # grammar (N9) already ruled it and the retired-id ledger below states it
    # verbatim: "replica grammar: origin catalog, carrier snowflake".
    #
    # WHAT MAKES THE ORIGIN UNAMBIGUOUS DESPITE THE CARRIER: the replica's
    # views PRESERVE THE SERVICENOW TABLE NAMES (a `V_`-prefixed view per
    # ServiceNow table — cmdb_ci, sys_user_group, core_company, sys_choice,
    # and the scoped-app extension tables under ServiceNow's own `x_<scope>_`
    # convention). A view name that is a ServiceNow table name is a ServiceNow
    # table, whatever database it is sitting in. Name the dataset for the
    # ServiceNow table, never for the Snowflake view wrapper.
    #
    # Mechanism only: the replica host, database, schema and any real
    # application/CI identifiers are Internal and stay company-side.
    disambiguation: "SNOW = ServiceNow (ITSM/CMDB). Distinct from system `snowflake` (the data platform). ServiceNow metadata is read from a Snowflake REPLICA — same pattern as Control-M read from the Oracle psgmgr replica — so origin stays `snow` and Snowflake is the carrier."
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"
    cmdb_ci: ~
    layer: technology
    classification: Internal
    binding: ~                          # no connection binding; the REASON is
                                        # declared in source-bindings.yaml `unbound:`
    locator:
      hosting: saas                     # Q4 ruling 2026-07-31: registers NOW, typed SaaS
    sdlc: ~
    notes: >
      Registered at the N7 gate (Q4). First dataset = snow:cmdb-ci-classes,
      which doubles as the crosswalk source for every system row's cmdb_ci
      field.

  - id: autosys
    name: "AutoSys (CA/Broadcom) — placeholder orchestrator"
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"
    cmdb_ci: ~
    layer: technology
    classification: Internal
    binding: ~                          # no connection binding; the REASON is
                                        # declared in source-bindings.yaml `unbound:`
    locator: {}
    sdlc: ~
    notes: "Crosswalk-only activation; no export feed exists (external/orchestration/autosys/)."

  - id: airflow
    name: "AWS Airflow / MWAA — placeholder orchestrator"
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"
    cmdb_ci: ~
    layer: technology
    classification: Internal
    binding: ~                          # no connection binding; the REASON is
                                        # declared in source-bindings.yaml `unbound:`
    locator:
      # THE POINTER, NEVER THE VALUE (internal/README.md): the internal MWAA
      # implementation-docs URL is a real internal address and lives ONLY in the
      # file below. Distinct from the apache.org `publisher_url` on the `apache`
      # vendor row in config/taxonomy/software-registry.yaml — that says who
      # PUBLISHES Airflow; this says where OUR deployment is documented.
      internal_docs: internal/airflow-reference/mwaa-internal-docs.md   # id airflow:internal-implementation-docs
    sdlc: ~
    notes: "Crosswalk-only activation; no DAG-export feed exists (external/orchestration/airflow/)."

  - id: dpl
    name: "DPL pipeline/dataset taxonomy registry"
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"
    cmdb_ci: ~
    layer: technology
    classification: Internal            # confidential handling: real SEAL ids + pipeline/dataset GUIDs
    binding: ~                          # no connection binding; the REASON is
                                        # declared in source-bindings.yaml `unbound:`
    locator:
      data_root: "DRYDOCS_DATA_ROOT (MANDATORY since G81 (d) -- no default); dpl-registry/<seal>/ = per-SEAL exports"
      resolver: drydocs_core/data_root.py   # dpl_registry_dir() (the G19 shared helper)
    sdlc: ~
    notes: >
      THE POINTER, NEVER THE DATA: per-SEAL Swagger exports carry real SEAL
      ids, GUIDs and lifecycle state and never enter the repo tree; fixtures
      are SYNTHETIC (G25).

  - id: snowflake
    name: "Snowflake (data platform)"
    # SNOWFLAKE IS THE DATA PLATFORM. NOT `snow` — that is ServiceNow, above.
    # This id has ALREADY caused one collision: the flat dataset id `snowflake`
    # was retired at v2 because it collided with this SYSTEM id (see the
    # retired-id ledger: "the flat id collided with the v2 SYSTEM id").
    # Appears as an ORIGIN only for things BORN here (a Snowflake-native schema
    # inventory). When it merely HOLDS another system's data it is the CARRIER
    # and the origin stays that system — precedent verbatim from the ledger:
    # "replica grammar: origin catalog, carrier snowflake".
    # THE CARRIER ROLE IS THE COMMON CASE, not the exception. Snowflake is this
    # estate's replica surface the way Oracle `psgmgr` is Control-M's: the
    # ServiceNow metadata this repo will read arrives through a Snowflake
    # replica, and stays `origin: snow`. Read `psgmgr` : Control-M as
    # `snowflake` : ServiceNow and the grammar answers itself.
    disambiguation: "Snowflake = the data platform. Distinct from system `snow` (ServiceNow). Usually the CARRIER (the estate's replica surface, as Oracle psgmgr is for Control-M); origin only for Snowflake-native data."
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"
    cmdb_ci: ~
    layer: data
    classification: Internal
    binding: snowflake-catalog            # -> config/source-bindings.yaml (G125); the profile names
                                        # the VARIABLES, never a value
    locator: {}
    sdlc: ~
    notes: "Carrier for the catalog@... registration views; per-schema data expansion is a future gate."

  - id: catalog
    name: "Enterprise data catalog (dataset/distribution registration)"
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"
    cmdb_ci: ~
    layer: data
    classification: Internal            # confidential handling: real dataset names, GUIDs, app ids, contacts, buckets, URIs
    binding: ~                          # no connection binding; the REASON is
                                        # declared in source-bindings.yaml `unbound:`
    locator:
      data_root: "DRYDOCS_DATA_ROOT (MANDATORY since G81 (d) -- no default); catalog/ = view exports, catalog/screenshots/ = evidence captures (confidential, never in-tree even gitignored)"
      resolver: drydocs_core/data_root.py   # catalog_dir() (the G19 shared helper)
    sdlc: ~
    notes: >
      The registration system whose curated views we read FROM Snowflake (the
      carrier) — origin catalog, carrier snowflake, exactly the replica case
      the @ grammar exists for (G42 seam).

  - id: exec-hosts
    name: "Control-M execution hosts (rua collector)"
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"
    cmdb_ci: ~
    layer: technology
    classification: Internal            # confidential handling: bundles hold real hostnames, uids, home paths, script copies
    binding: ~                          # no connection binding; the REASON is
                                        # declared in source-bindings.yaml `unbound:`
    locator:
      data_root: "DRYDOCS_DATA_ROOT (MANDATORY since G81 (d) -- no default); rua/incoming/ = tarballs, rua/extracted/<bundle>/ = unpacked"
      resolver: drydocs_core/data_root.py   # the ONE shared helper (G19)
    sdlc: ~
    notes: >
      THE POINTER, NEVER THE DATA: bundle payloads are confidential and never
      enter the repo tree (guard: tests/unit/test_data_root.py); transport is
      the internal-local hand-carry note (G19).

  - id: bitbucket
    name: "Company code repositories (Bitbucket/GitHub)"
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"
    cmdb_ci: ~
    layer: technology
    classification: Internal            # real repo/branch names + script paths; content stays company-side
    binding: ~                          # no connection binding; the REASON is
                                        # declared in source-bindings.yaml `unbound:`
    locator: {}
    sdlc: ~
    notes: >
      A repo is a valid truth source ONLY where a team keeps a clean branch
      (trusted_ref on the dataset row); production servers hold the latest
      DEPLOYED code (G24).
      WORDING CORRECTED 2026-08-06 (gate rua-load-shapes §E1, SME): this note
      used to say servers "always run the latest RUNNING code". Deployed is NOT
      running — a script may have been deployed to the WRONG SERVER, in which
      case it is present, called by nothing on that host, and dead in place.
      The server extract is truth for what is deployed and WHERE, nothing more.

  - id: oracle
    name: "Oracle DB schemas (data platform, placeholder)"
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"
    cmdb_ci: ~
    layer: data
    classification: Internal            # confidential handling: real schema/table/object names
    binding: oracle-inventory            # -> config/source-bindings.yaml (G125); the profile names
                                        # the VARIABLES, never a value
    locator: {}
    sdlc: ~
    notes: "Per-schema system split + datasets per table group are a future gate (migration sketch row)."

  - id: drydocs-stg
    name: "DryDocs staging schema (our own derived store)"
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"
    cmdb_ci: ~
    layer: data
    classification: Internal
    binding: oracle-drydocs-stg            # -> config/source-bindings.yaml (G125); the profile names
                                        # the VARIABLES, never a value
    locator:
      schema: drydocs_stg               # our own staging schema (mechanism; committed in v1 too)
    sdlc: docs/reviews/sdlc-oracle-ingestion.md
    notes: "Holds the C3/C4 normalizer outputs (derived stores — Q3: derived: true, authority omitted)."

  - id: repo
    name: "The DryDocs repo itself (repo-committed ledgers + derived captures)"
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"
    cmdb_ci: ~
    layer: technology
    classification: Internal-Public     # the repo's own committed artifacts; per-dataset notes tighten where needed
    binding: ~                          # no connection binding; the REASON is
                                        # declared in source-bindings.yaml `unbound:`
    locator: {}
    sdlc: ~
    notes: "Born-here datasets: the software-registry ledger, depgraph snapshots, design docs (tenant 0)."

  - id: infra
    name: "Infrastructure inventory site (per-application server export)"
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"
    cmdb_ci: ~
    layer: technology
    classification: Internal            # confidential handling: real hostnames, racks, building locations, owning-app identifiers
    binding: ~                          # no connection binding; the REASON is
                                        # declared in source-bindings.yaml `unbound:`
    locator:
      hosting: internal-web             # an internal inventory UI; the site name/URL live ONLY in the internal/ twin (pointer-never-the-value)
      drop_readme: internal/server-inventory/README.md   # the landing zone's tracked procedure doc (Z1)
    sdlc: ~
    notes: >
      The internal site whose per-business-application server export feeds
      Epic Z (server location & geography). PROVENANCE: whether this site
      ORIGINATES server/placement facts or fronts a CMDB (which would make it
      ADS, not SOR) is not established — gate server-location-ontology §C4
      (SIGNED 2026-08-19) keeps authority: SOR with the caveat and
      PRE-AUTHORIZES the evidence-based flip to ADS as an update-not-ruling:
      when a company-side confirmation of what backs the site lands, record
      it here and flip, no re-gate. Mechanism only: no site name, URL,
      hostname or rack value here.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DATASETS — what loaders read and gates rule. `confirmed` is PER DATASET.
# `urn` is DERIVED (never written here). `replaces` back-points the retired
# v1 flat id (D4).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
datasets:
  # ---- Control-M replica datasets in psgmgr (origin controlm = SOR, carrier
  # ---- psgmgr = ADS). Column ledger: config/source-mappings/psgmgr.yaml.
  - id: "controlm@[db].psgmgr.cm_def_vtab"
    system: psgmgr
    origin: controlm
    artifact: cm_def_vtab
    artifact_kind: table
    taxonomy_category: Pipelines
    asset_type: dcat:Dataset
    authority: ADS
    feeds_taxonomy: [folders]
    adapter: oracle
    cadence: batch                 # G79: how OFTEN it refreshes -- moves with the Control-M estate, so every scheduled ingest wants it
    acquisition:                        # N12 (2026-08-18): how the data arrives
      mode: automated
      via: db                           # the row's own id names the qualified object
    locator:
      mapping: config/source-mappings/psgmgr.yaml
    confirmed: true                     # gate controlm-q1q3-phase1 (2026-07-07) — transfers per Q6
    replaces: controlm-psgmgr
    notes: >
      Folders (replicated DEF_VTAB). Loader controlm_folders.v1 (+ the
      CM_DEF_VJOB folder HEADER ROW join for APPLICATION — gate q1q3 §Q3).

  - id: "controlm@[db].psgmgr.cm_def_vjob"
    system: psgmgr
    origin: controlm
    artifact: cm_def_vjob
    artifact_kind: table
    taxonomy_category: Pipelines
    asset_type: dcat:Dataset
    authority: ADS
    feeds_taxonomy: [jobs]
    adapter: oracle
    cadence: batch                 # G79: how OFTEN it refreshes -- moves with the Control-M estate, so every scheduled ingest wants it
    acquisition:                        # N12 (2026-08-18): how the data arrives
      mode: automated
      via: db                           # the row's own id names the qualified object
    locator:
      mapping: config/source-mappings/psgmgr.yaml
    confirmed: true                     # gate controlm-q1q3-phase1 (2026-07-07) — transfers per Q6
    replaces: controlm-psgmgr
    notes: >
      Job definitions — the SME's own worked example for the amended Q1
      grammar (controlm@[db].[schema].cm_def_vjob). Audit envelope confirmed
      (config/audit-fields.yaml). job.APPLICATION is NOT reliable SEAL
      identity (K1) — SEAL attribution rides the stg_app_fact dataset.

  - id: "controlm@[db].psgmgr.cm_def_lnki_p_vw"
    system: psgmgr
    origin: controlm
    artifact: cm_def_lnki_p_vw
    artifact_kind: view
    taxonomy_category: Pipelines
    asset_type: dcat:Dataset
    authority: ADS
    feeds_taxonomy: [conditions, dependencies]
    adapter: oracle
    cadence: batch                 # G79: how OFTEN it refreshes -- moves with the Control-M estate, so every scheduled ingest wants it
    acquisition:                        # N12 (2026-08-18): how the data arrives
      mode: automated
      via: db                           # the row's own id names the qualified object
    locator:
      mapping: config/source-mappings/psgmgr.yaml
    confirmed: true                     # gate controlm-q1q3-phase1 (2026-07-07) — transfers per Q6
    replaces: controlm-psgmgr
    notes: >
      IN-conditions. Also the anchor dataset for the derived WAS_INFORMED_BY
      pairing (controlm_dependencies_derived.v1 joins this view to the OUT
      view on condition name — recorded here, per-row residual 2026-07-31).

  - id: "controlm@[db].psgmgr.cm_def_lnko_p_vw"
    system: psgmgr
    origin: controlm
    artifact: cm_def_lnko_p_vw
    artifact_kind: view
    taxonomy_category: Pipelines
    asset_type: dcat:Dataset
    authority: ADS
    feeds_taxonomy: [conditions]
    adapter: oracle
    cadence: batch                 # G79: how OFTEN it refreshes -- moves with the Control-M estate, so every scheduled ingest wants it
    acquisition:                        # N12 (2026-08-18): how the data arrives
      mode: automated
      via: db                           # the row's own id names the qualified object
    locator:
      mapping: config/source-mappings/psgmgr.yaml
    confirmed: true                     # gate controlm-q1q3-phase1 (2026-07-07) — transfers per Q6
    replaces: controlm-psgmgr

  - id: "controlm@[db].psgmgr.cm_def_setvar_vw"
    system: psgmgr
    origin: controlm
    artifact: cm_def_setvar_vw
    artifact_kind: view
    taxonomy_category: Pipelines
    asset_type: dcat:Dataset
    authority: ADS
    feeds_taxonomy: [variables]
    adapter: oracle
    acquisition:                        # N12 (2026-08-18): how the data arrives
      mode: automated
      via: db                           # the row's own id names the qualified object
    locator:
      mapping: config/source-mappings/psgmgr.yaml
    confirmed: true                     # covered by controlm-q1q3-phase1 (the five psgmgr extracts) + the C3/C4 normalization gates — transfers per Q6
    replaces: controlm-psgmgr

      Folder/job variables — the C3/C4 Python-normalizer input feeding the

  - id: "controlm@[db].psgmgr.cm_hosts"
    system: psgmgr
    origin: controlm
    artifact: cm_hosts
    artifact_kind: table
    taxonomy_category: Infrastructure
    asset_type: dcat:Dataset

    acquisition:                        # N12 (2026-08-18): how the data arrives

      via: db                           # the row's own id names the qualified object

      mapping: config/source-mappings/psgmgr.yaml

# + `decided_by` (gate id in config/gate-log.md). `status: stub` marks a
# registered source whose envelope gate has not run; loaders must not write
# envelope properties for stub sources.

# Ontology note: the envelope properties are property-level provenance,
# bound to standard terms at gate envelope-property-terms (2026-08-04, M4):
# dct:creator / dct:created / dct:modified / dct:contributor — registered in
# the property_terms section of relationship_vocabulary.yaml.

surfaces.title: Precedence
surfaces.content:
# =============================================================================
# config/precedence.yaml — source-of-truth ordering for the configuration layer.
#
# When sources disagree about what something IS, resolve top-down. The first
# authority that has an opinion wins; lower authorities become aliases
# (skos:closeMatch / recorded note), never silent overrides.
#
# Edit `order:` to change which authority is consulted first. The HITL gate
# surfaces every conflict this file resolves so the SME can confirm.
# =============================================================================

schema: drydocs.precedence.v1
updated: 2026-07-15   # K4 clause 7 — seal-pat-source-of-record wired into the live chain

# The ordered authority chain. Lower index = higher authority.
order:
  - id: bmc-baseline
    authority: 1
    role: orchestration-vendor-baseline
    governs: [Folder, Job, Condition, dependency, calendar, execution-host, run-as-user]
    source: external/orchestration/bmc-controlm/
    rationale: >
      BMC Control-M is the canonical orchestrator. Its object semantics are ground truth;
      other orchestrators (AutoSys, Airflow) crosswalk TO these concepts.

  - id: internal-standards
    authority: 2
    role: company-convention
    governs: [naming, data-center-codes, folder-naming, calendar-resolution, description-fields]
    source: knowledge/standards/
    rationale: >
      Company conventions that refine the baseline for our environment. They normalize and
      disambiguate baseline values but do not redefine baseline concepts.

  - id: seal-pat-source-of-record
    authority: 3
    role: internal-source-of-record
    governs: [internal-product-identity, internal-business-identity, application-fact-provenance]
    source: "drydocs-docmeta scraped SEAL/PAT corpus (component pending; see knowledge/upgrade-plans/docmeta-component.md)"
    rationale: >
      SEAL/PAT scraped documentation is the authoritative source for internal product/business
      IDENTITY — when a scraped SEAL/PAT fact conflicts with the catalog/PAT taxonomy on what
      an internal application/product IS (not who owns it), SEAL/PAT wins. Placed ABOVE
      lob-product-team because its identity claims must beat the catalog's; ownership/
      business-context stays with lob-product-team (disjoint governs). WIRED at K4 clause 7
      (2026-07-15; gate 2026-07-10 §D sign-off) from the former proposed_additions block.
      No feed exists until drydocs-docmeta ships — the authority is live but silent.

  - id: lob-product-team
    authority: 4
    role: org-taxonomy
    governs: [ownership, business-context, LOB, ProductLine, Product, AreaProduct, DevTeam]
    source: internal/org/        # confidential rosters live here
    rationale: >
      The org taxonomy assigns ownership and business context. Lowest authority for object
      *meaning*, but the sole authority for *who owns it* — used to attach context, not to
      redefine orchestration objects.

  # ---- G72: the TOM attribution surfaces (gate tom-roles-enumeration-and-
  # cardinality, SIGNED 2026-08-11, SS-D3/SS-D4). THE SURFACES ARE THREE, not the
  # two SS-D1 described, and every Attribution stamps `source` with its
  # surface's `stamp:` below — so a roster disagreement ("five Operate
  # Managers?") is a READABLE fact: which surface said so. Disjoint `governs`
  # from everything above; the SS-D4 order is hand-verified > ServiceNow TOM >
  # SEAL extract (human verification outranks both automated surfaces; the
  # operating-model source outranks the contact extract).
  #
  # NEVER-READ vs DID-NOT-ASSERT (the O44 alluvial's ribbon-stop): this block
  # declares which surfaces EXIST; whether one was READ is a load-record fact
  # (the loader's :JobRun rows, or — for the two company-side surfaces — the
  # loader's very existence on that side). An Attribution absent FROM a read
  # surface means "did not assert". A diagram cannot draw a difference the
  # data does not carry, and this declaration is the half the data carries.
  #
  # SS-E1g CHECKED BEFORE BUILDING (evidence doc section 10.3): ServiceNow's
  # Direct rows carry `u_source` naming the feed INTO ServiceNow (e.g. the
  # SEAL deployment-contacts feed). That discriminates ServiceNow's own row
  # provenance — it complements this vocabulary (the TOM loader should carry
  # it through as its own property) but it cannot name the OTHER two
  # surfaces, so it does not replace the discriminator ruled here.
  - id: hand-verified-crosswalk
    authority: 5
    role: attribution-surface
    governs: [tom-attribution-roster]
    stamp: HAND_VERIFIED
    source: "company-side hand-verified crosswalk (gate snow-hpsm-queue-to-group; per-machine, gitignored)"
    rationale: >
      Human verification outranks both automated surfaces (SS-D4). Trust rides the
      crosswalk's EXISTING verification vocabulary — verified / cert_status /
      cert_next_date — reused rather than minted (the cmdb_rel_type descriptor-column
      discipline). COMPANY-SIDE ONLY (RELAY-6): the producer repo cannot load this
      surface, and that is exactly why the discriminator must be able to NAME a
      surface this repo cannot itself read.

  - id: servicenow-tom
    authority: 6
    role: attribution-surface
    governs: [tom-attribution-roster]
    stamp: SERVICENOW_TOM
    source: "ServiceNow TOM Accountable view (company replica; knowledge/upgrade-plans/servicenow-replica-evidence.md)"
    rationale: >
      The operating-model source outranks the contact extract (SS-D4). Not ingested
      producer-side; declared so its rows are attributable the day the company loader
      lands, and so a SEAL-vs-TOM count difference reads as two surfaces disagreeing
      rather than one roster mutating. Direct rows carry u_source (SS-E1g) — pass it
      through on the Attribution when that loader is built.

  - id: seal-contact-extract
    authority: 7
    role: attribution-surface
    governs: [tom-attribution-roster]
    stamp: SEAL
    source: "SEAL application-info + contact extracts (drydocs/loaders/cypher/seal_applications.cypher, seal_contacts.cypher)"
    rationale: >
      The one surface loaded producer-side today; BOTH loader sites stamp this
      surface. The stamp is deliberately the literal 'SEAL' every already-loaded
      graph carries and the pinned 4-part attribution_id embeds (app_id|SEAL|role|sid,
      identity gate SS-D2) — declaring the existing value costs zero migration and
      keeps property and key telling one story. (The PAT team-role attributions are a
      different fact family and already stamp 'pat' — not part of this roster.)

# How conflicts are recorded when a lower authority disagrees with a higher one.
conflict_policy:
  winner: highest-authority
  loser_disposition: alias        # record as skos:closeMatch / note on the edge or node
  require_sme_confirmation: true  # the guided gate shows every conflict before it is applied
  never: silent-drop

# Toggle which authorities are active (e.g. disable a feed during onboarding).
active:
  bmc-baseline: true
  internal-standards: true
  seal-pat-source-of-record: true   # live but silent until the docmeta corpus feeds it
  lob-product-team: true
  hand-verified-crosswalk: true     # live but silent — company-side surface (G72)
  servicenow-tom: true              # live but silent — company loader not built (G72)
  seal-contact-extract: true

# =============================================================================
# History: the seal-pat-source-of-record authority above was PROPOSED at the
# 2026-07-08 review as an inert `proposed_additions:` block, gate-confirmed
# 2026-07-10 (config/gate-prompts/seal-tom-attribution-reshape.yaml §D), and
# WIRED into the live `order:`/`active:` chain at K4 clause 7 (2026-07-15).
# The linked mechanism is prov:hadPrimarySource on every extracted fact —
# config/taxonomy-ontology-map.yaml#seal-doc-source-of-record (confirmed) and
# relationship_vocabulary/#business_application_had_primary_source (active, edge-only;
# id migrated from seal_had_primary_source at G101, 2026-08-21).
# =============================================================================

surfaces.title: Sensitivity classification
surfaces.content:
# =============================================================================
# config/classification.yaml — sensitivity classification (the THIRD axis).
#
# DryDocs ingestion carries three independent axes:
#   (1) precedence authority — which source wins on conflict   (config/precedence.yaml)
#   (2) provenance tier       — TRUST: vendor's words vs Claude inference
#                               (VERBATIM / GROUNDED / SYNTHESIZED, decided at
#                                ingestion, recorded in each SOURCE-MANIFEST)
#   (3) sensitivity classification — THIS file: who may see it / may it be published
#
# The classification is DECIDED AT INGESTION TIME and recorded per source. It drives
# the GitHub publish boundary (PUBLISH-BOUNDARY.md) like a .gitignore: the
# non-publishable tiers never enter a public push.
# =============================================================================

schema: drydocs.classification.v1
updated: 2026-07-31        # J23: Internal-Confidential collapsed into Internal (3 levels; a 4th tier can return if a real handling difference ever materializes)

levels:
  - id: External
    rank: 0
    publishable: true
    description: >
      Publicly available third-party material — vendor docs fetched from a public URL,
      ontology standards, academic research.
    homes: [reference/, external/]
    requires: [source_url, captured_at]      # External => must cite the public URL + fetch date

  - id: Internal-Public                       # "Internal-Public Availability"
    rank: 1
    publishable: true
    description: >
      Internally authored but cleared for public availability — design prose, ontology
      docs, generic naming standards. Contains no confidential identifiers.
    homes: [knowledge/]

  - id: Internal
    rank: 2
    publishable: false
    description: >
      Internal-only — NOT for public GitHub, never leaves the private repo. Operational
      metadata, internal process docs, AND confidential material (real rosters, SIDs,
      SEAL ids, schema object names) — the former Internal-Confidential tier collapsed
      into this level (user ruling 2026-07-31, J23): the private repo + publish boundary
      is the protection, and the extra tier's pointer-never-the-data discipline was
      preventing internal/ from holding the values the work needs. Where a source is
      confidential, say so in a handling note on the entry. Real secrets/credentials
      still never commit anywhere; large or PII-bearing payloads may stay out-of-tree
      per source (noted on the entry), no longer tier-forced.
    homes: [internal/]

# The GitHub publish boundary (a .gitignore-style guard).
publish_rule:
  publish_when: "level.publishable == true"            # External + Internal-Public
  exclude_from_public_push: [Internal]
  enforced_by: "PUBLISH-BOUNDARY.md (+ .gitignore on the public remote)"
  note: >
    The directory layout aligns with this — reference/ + external/ + knowledge/ are
    publishable; internal/ is not — but the per-source `classification` label is the
    authoritative driver of what is excluded from a public push.

# Required on EVERY ingested source (a data feed OR a document corpus).
required_on_every_source:
  - classification      # one of levels[].id — in config/source-registry.yaml (feeds)
                        #   and in each SOURCE-MANIFEST (document corpora)
  - source              # the system/path the data came from (e.g. oracle:psgmgr)
required_for_external:  # additionally, when classification == External:
  - source_url          # the public URL the content was fetched from
  - captured_at         # the ingestion / fetch date

# NB: this axis is SENSITIVITY, not TRUST. The provenance tier
# (VERBATIM/GROUNDED/SYNTHESIZED) lives in each SOURCE-MANIFEST and answers a
# different question (is this the vendor's words or Claude's inference?).

# Publish ceiling — ce-wilson/DryDocs is PRIVATE (verified via gh, 2026-07-18;
# an earlier revision of this comment wrongly said "public") but SOMETIMES
# PUBLISHED (CLAUDE.md §3), so treat every tracked file as publishable-eventually:
# Internal-Public stays the maximum tier for tracked files; everything Internal or
# above lives in a gitignored twin (drydocs/data/ etc.).
# drydocs/data/samples/** is synthetic-only (no standing exceptions). The two
# pre-boundary seal_*__sample.csv twins (tracked 2026-05-18, real seal_ids with
# fictional names) were DELETED from the tip 2026-07-19 (user call); git HISTORY
# retains them until a history rewrite — the residual reason any public
# publication of this repo's history remains user-gated.
public_producer:
  ceiling_tier: Internal-Public
  flow: one-way               # public → internal; never pulled back via git

# Sanitization map — how to demote a higher-tier value to Internal-Public so a
# doc or fixture can be committed to this repo.
sanitize:
  real_seal_or_app_id:   "<seal-id> / <app-id>"
  real_lob_product_name: "<LoB> or a generic role (e.g. 'a cards LoB')"
  real_system_codename:  "generic functional name (e.g. 'Business Catalog')"
  real_infra_object:     "placeholder or synthetic example"
  # J13 class 2 (SME 2026-08-11). Control-M data-center names, application codes
  # and job names encode the ENVIRONMENT in position 1. Swap that one character
  # to the non-production letter and the identifier stops naming a live object
  # while every parsing rule still reads true — the grammar is the publishable
  # part, the environment value is not. Guarded by Scan E in
  # tests/unit/test_publish_boundary_values.py. Real values: internal twin
  # internal/standards/technology/data-center-inventory.md.
  production_env_identifier: "swap position-1 environment letter (P -> T)"
  # NOT a sanitize rule but the boundary beside it: per-data-center VOLUMETRICS
  # (folder/job counts) are a distinct class and are NOT ruled publishable —
  # totals stay, the per-DC split goes to the internal twin. See gate-log
  # 2026-08-11 RECORD.
  roster_row:            "synthetic name, or omit"
  internal_ghe_repo_id:  "<internal-ghe>"
  real_location_row:     "synthetic or omit"

# Paths that are Internal-only regardless of content — never port outward.
excluded_paths:
  - ".github/skills/**"
  - ".vscode/**"
  - "drydocs/data/**"              # gitignored — real source/sample data + internal twins
  - "stg_out/"                     # gitignored — extract/staging output (real data)
  - "stg_*/"
  - "team_locations__sample.csv"   # real location rows, even if non-PII
  - "docs/design/feedback/scans/**"  # gitignored — raw paper-HITL scans (Epic L / L6);
                                      # Internal by default, see scans/README.md; the
                                      # ANCHOR-KEYED TRANSCRIPTION derived from a scan
                                      # (docs/design/feedback/<doc>-rev<N>.yaml) is a
                                      # separate, publishable-by-default artifact — not
                                      # covered by this exclusion
