surfaces.title: Doc-capture policy (page ceiling, delay, scheme allow-list)
surfaces.content:
# =============================================================================
# config/doc-capture.yaml — the ONE doc-capture policy (Q12).
#
# Q12's acceptance is explicit that "the threshold and the per-request delay
# are config values, never hardcoded literals", and the reason is that these
# numbers are POLICY about how we treat a third party, not implementation
# detail of one script. Two consumers read this file:
#
#   * scripts/external_vendor_scrape.py — the standalone vendor capture
#   * drydocs_docmeta/connectors/web.py — the component's generic web connector
#
# One file so the two cannot drift into different notions of "too many pages",
# which would make the guardrail depend on which entrypoint the operator
# happened to use.
#
# WHY A CEILING AT ALL — the numbers are measured, not guessed (2026-07-31,
# from the publishers' own toc.json, so the count is knowable BEFORE any
# content request):
#   documents.bmc.com /supportu/INC/      10,912 pages  ~210 MB
#   documents.bmc.com /supportu/9.0.20/    3,860 pages   ~74 MB
#   documents.bmc.com /supportu/9.0.21/    1,965 pages   ~38 MB
# Three harms the refusal prevents: hammering a vendor whose robots.txt ALLOWS
# these paths (so politeness is entirely ours, hence the delay); committing
# tens of MB of vendor copyright into a repo that is private-but-sometimes-
# published; and the operator picking the WRONG TREE and not noticing —
# /supportu/INC/ is the INCONTROL MAINFRAME family, whose "Control-M" subtree
# is Control-M for z/OS, not the distributed estate DryDocs models.
# =============================================================================

schema: drydocs.doc-capture.v1
updated: 2026-08-04

capture:
  # Refuse a capture larger than this unless the operator raises it explicitly.
  # Deliberately well BELOW every real tree above, so the default answer to an
  # unsized run is "stop" rather than "probably fine".
  max_pages: 600

  # Seconds between content requests. There is no server-side backstop on the
  # paths we capture, so this is the whole of our politeness.
  delay_seconds: 1.0

  timeout_seconds: 30
  retries: 3

  # Identifies the fetcher to the vendor rather than impersonating a browser.
  user_agent: "DryDocs-docs-capture/1.0 (+internal knowledge-graph research; contact repo owner)"

  # SSRF allow-list. A doc capture has no business reaching file://, ftp://,
  # gopher:// or a data: URI, and http(s) is the whole of what a public vendor
  # documentation site speaks. Anything else is either a mistake or an attempt
  # to make the fetcher read something local.
  allowed_schemes:
    - https
    - http

surfaces.title: Data zones (path modes + the non-overlap invariant)
surfaces.content:
# =============================================================================
# config/data-zones.yaml — every path the system may WRITE, declared with a mode
# =============================================================================
# G81, 2026-08-23. THE INCIDENT: an internal folder holding extracted CSV source
# data was OVERWRITTEN (2026-08-11). Recovered from backup, so nothing was
# permanently lost — but the class stays live until a write path and a source
# drop path can no longer be the same place by accident. The full reconstruction,
# including the four measured overlaps that existed when this file was written,
# is docs/reviews/g81-data-path-reconstruction.md.
#
# WHY A CONFIG FILE AND NOT PYTHON. Before this, a path was whatever one of
# twelve helpers in drydocs_core/data_root.py returned. Nothing distinguished a
# folder the system OWNS from a folder a human DROPS INTO — that lived only in
# docstrings — and no reader could enumerate what the system touches without
# reading every helper and its call sites. That is why an overlap stayed
# invisible until it destroyed something.
#
# THE INVARIANT (tests/unit/test_data_zones.py, and it is the whole defect in one
# sentence): NO write-mode path may equal, contain, OR BE CONTAINED BY a
# read-mode path. Both directions — the acceptance named only one, and two of the
# four live findings ran the other way (see the reconstruction §3).
#
# WHY A WRITE ZONE HAS NO SOURCE-REGISTRY ROW (G109 (a), recorded rather than
# fixed). The registry declares SOURCES — where data ARRIVES from and drops in.
# A write or scratch zone is an output the system owns; it has no provenance, no
# trust axis and no acquisition mode, so a registry row for one would be a field
# set of nulls asserting a source that does not exist. That is the "recorded
# reason a zone legitimately has none" branch, and it covers rua-extracted,
# remediation-outgoing, remediation-recommendations, vendor-docs, context-intake,
# cmdline-staging and run-logs. What G109 fixed instead was the READ SURFACE:
# `drydocs landing-zones` used to read only the registry, so every zone in this
# file was invisible to the one command that answers "are my extracts still
# there". It now reports both declarations and --check covers the read zones of
# each. Mode decides what EMPTY means — an empty read zone is missing source
# data, an empty write zone is a directory the system rebuilds.
#
# READ ZONES ARE NOT DECLARED HERE when they are dataset drops. Those already
# live in config/source-registry.yaml as `acquisition.drop_dir` (N12), resolved
# by drydocs_core/landing_zones.py; duplicating them would create exactly the
# drift this repo keeps killing. The invariant JOINS the two files. Only a read
# zone that is NOT a dataset drop (an evidence area, a per-fix working drop) is
# declared here, and the guard fails if a zone here duplicates a registry row.
#
# MODES
#   read     source data a human drops in. The system may NEVER write it, and
#            its helper cannot create, clean or write (G81 (e)).
#   write    outputs the system owns and may rebuild. May create.
#   scratch  disposable working space. May create and clean.
#
# BASES — where `path` is rooted. Never a real machine path (the J15 rule:
# enumerate the shape, never the values; real paths live in the internal twin).
#   data_root  under DRYDOCS_DATA_ROOT. Since G81 (d) that variable is MANDATORY:
#              unset or empty FAILS naming it, rather than silently relocating
#              every zone to ~/data/DryDocs.
#   home       under the user's home directory (the run-log idiom).
#   repo       in the working tree. The spelling matches landing_zones.BASE_REPO
#              on purpose -- the two declarations join in overlaps(), so one base
#              meaning "the repo" in one file and nothing in the other is a seam
#              waiting to be misread. G126 added it.
#
# IN-TREE ZONES PAY A PRICE: `rebuild`. A repo-based zone is reachable by
# `git clean -fdx` no matter what .gitignore says, so it must say how an operator
# gets its contents back from nothing. A landing zone earns its in-tree place by
# holding TRACKED files (tests/unit/test_landing_zones.py); a zone here that is
# ignored and untracked -- console-credentials is the one -- earns it by
# declaring a one-command rebuild instead. Not a blanket exception: the guard
# fails a new in-tree zone that declares neither.
schema: drydocs.data-zones.v1

zones:
  # ---- rua bundles (G19) ----------------------------------------------------
  # The pair this item exists to separate. `rua/incoming/` is the READ half and
  # is declared in the source registry (exec-hosts:rua-bundle), whose drop_dir
  # was corrected from the over-broad `rua/` to `rua/incoming/` at G81 — the
  # narrowing this file's invariant requires, and what data_root.py's own module
  # docstring has said since G19.
  - id: rua-extracted
    mode: write
    base: data_root
    path: rua/extracted/
    helper: rua_extracted_dir
    note: >
      Unpack area, one directory per bundle. THE OVERWRITE PRIMITIVE lives here:
      rua_inventory._unpack calls tarfile.extractall, which overwrites existing
      files with no warning and no diff, into a directory named after the
      tarball's own basename. It is legitimately rebuilt by a re-run, which is
      exactly why it must never sit inside the zone the bundles are dropped into.

  # ---- remediation (the fix-package lifecycle) ------------------------------
  # incoming is a READ zone with no dataset row: per-fix working copies of folder
  # .xml exports, dropped by hand. Deliberately separate from the controlm-xml
  # INGESTION zone so that "which exports are loaded?" stays answerable.
  - id: remediation-incoming
    mode: read
    base: data_root
    path: remediation/incoming/
    helper: remediation_incoming_dir
    note: >
      Hand-dropped folder exports awaiting a remediation pass. Not a dataset drop
      (no source-registry row): its lifecycle is the fix package, not the graph
      load. Read-mode, so its helper cannot create — a missing zone is reported,
      never silently made.

  - id: remediation-outgoing
    mode: write
    base: data_root
    path: remediation/outgoing/
    helper: remediation_outgoing_dir
    note: >
      Emitted <folder>.updated.xml minimal-diff artifacts that xml_io.write
      produced and self-checked; one fix package's target/ contents stage here.

  - id: remediation-recommendations
    mode: write
    base: data_root
    path: remediation/recommendations/
    helper: remediation_recommendations_dir
    note: >
      Recommendation documents — change docs, equivalence reports, fix-tracking
      change-sets awaiting the loader.

  # ---- system-written corpora ----------------------------------------------
  - id: vendor-docs
    mode: write
    base: data_root
    path: vendor-docs/
    helper: vendor_docs_dir
    note: >
      VERBATIM external-vendor documentation captures the SCRAPER writes
      (<tree>/pages/*.htm + capture-manifest.json). Write-mode because a capture
      run owns and rebuilds it; the vendor's words are re-fetchable, unlike a
      hand-carried source extract.

  - id: context-intake
    mode: write
    base: data_root
    path: context-intake/
    helper: context_intake_dir
    note: >
      O46 SME context-intake: the intake.db record store beside per-intake
      evidence directories. The system writes both. The 2026-08-06 storage ruling
      keys on this being ONE configured base path — records carry sha256 digests
      and relative keys only, so local -> share -> object store is a config
      change. Declaring it here is that ruling's mechanism, not a new one.

  # ---- human evidence drops (read, no dataset row) --------------------------
  - id: catalog-exports
    mode: read
    base: data_root
    path: catalog/
    helper: catalog_dir
    note: >
      G42 Snowflake data-catalog view exports plus the SME evidence screenshots
      under catalog/screenshots/. Hand-pulled: real dataset names, GUIDs, app
      ids, emails and buckets. Read-mode — the helper lost `create` at G81 (e),
      because a system that can make this directory can also land a write in it.

  - id: email-extracts
    mode: read
    base: data_root
    path: email-extracts/
    helper: email_extracts_dir
    note: >
      Q10 landing zone: Copilot JSON extracts beside their original .msg files,
      hand-exported. The repo carries only synthetic samples. Read-mode.

  # ---- staging + operator config (found while walking the call sites) -------
  - id: cmdline-staging
    mode: write
    base: data_root
    path: cmdline-staging/
    helper: cmdline_staging_dir
    note: >
      G39 job-detail staging store (SQLite). A TEMPORARY stand-in for the unbuilt
      psgmgr CM_DEF_VJOB_DETAIL table, rebuilt by export-cmdline-staging — the
      system owns it outright. Reached through source_dir() before G81 and so
      undeclared; found by walking the call sites, which is the audit the
      Python-side declaration made impossible.

  - id: controlm-api-config
    mode: read
    base: data_root
    path: controlm-api/
    helper: controlm_api_config_dir
    note: >
      Holds controlm_api.cfg — the G96 Control-M API adapter's endpoint/credential
      pointer, AUTHORED BY AN OPERATOR. Read-mode: the system consumes it and must
      never rewrite it, and overwriting an operator's credentials config is the
      same class as overwriting their extract.

  # ---- logs (the third family the SME named) -------------------------------
  - id: run-logs
    mode: write
    base: home
    path: logs/DryDocs/
    helper: ~   # drydocs_core.run_log owns this one; no data_root helper
    env: DRYDOCS_LOGDIR
    note: >
      ALL loader/supplement run logs. Declared here so the three families the SME
      named (logs, loader input, remediation output) are enumerable in one place.
      SCOPE FENCE: unlike the data root, this keeps its default — G81 (d) names
      the DATA root, and a relocated log is annoying where a relocated data root
      is destructive. A log may hold real source values (job names, rejected
      rows), which is why it is outside the repo either way.

  # ---- verbatim doc captures (G109 (e)) -------------------------------------
  - id: confluence-capture
    mode: read
    base: data_root
    path: confluence-capture/
    helper: ~   # arrives with the loader that reads it; declaring the zone does not need one
    note: >
      RULED AT G109 (e), which required this to be settled one way rather than
      left as an undocumented violation. The cdo-frameworks capture
      (config/doc-source-registry.yaml, VERBATIM, Internal) has been landing
      IN-TREE under internal/knowledge/data/<space>/. That is the most deletable
      state a payload can be in: untracked AND not gitignored, which `git clean
      -fd` removes without even needing -x. THE RULING IS "IT MOVES", not "the
      rule gains an exception", and the reason it cannot be an exception is that
      it could never expire — landing_zones.py permits an in-tree zone only when
      its contents are TRACKED, and PUBLISH-BOUNDARY.md forbids ever tracking a
      verbatim capture carrying real employee names and internal URLs. An
      exception here would be permanent by construction. Every sibling verbatim
      capture already lands out of tree for the same reason: vendor-docs/ exists
      precisely as "the external/ServiceNow/extracted/ .gitignore precedent
      generalized to a real out-of-repo home". Read-mode: the capture is the
      scrape's output and DryDocs' input, so nothing here may write it.
      COMPANY-SIDE NOTE, since that is where the scrape runs: producer has no
      internal/knowledge/ directory at all, so this ruling costs nothing to adopt
      here and is a real relocation only on the checkout that holds the capture.

  # ---- machine-local operator area (G126) -----------------------------------
  - id: console-credentials
    mode: read
    base: repo
    path: internal-local/
    helper: ~   # drydocs_api.credentials.credentials_path() owns it; no data_root helper
    rebuild: poetry run python scripts/set_console_credential.py <persona-id>
    note: >
      Holds console-credentials.json -- the web console's scrypt hashes, WRITTEN
      BY A PERSON at a no-echo prompt and read by the API. The exact shape of
      controlm-api-config above, and it takes the same mode for the same reason:
      READ means the SYSTEM may never write here, and the operator's hand is not
      the system. That is not a workaround for a missing dual mode -- it is the
      guarantee the console actually needs, and it already has a second enforcer
      pointing the same way (tests/unit/test_mapping_api.py forbids every
      filesystem write primitive inside drydocs_api, because an endpoint that can
      rewrite this file is an endpoint that can grant itself an account). A
      `write` declaration would contradict that guard, which is worse than no
      declaration at all.
      THE ZONE IS THE DIRECTORY, NOT THE FILE. Nothing in the system writes
      anywhere under internal-local/ -- verified by walking the call sites, the
      G81 method -- so the broad claim is the true one and it protects the
      deepdoc corpus and the Confluence scripts living beside the credentials.
      IN-TREE AND IGNORED, WHICH IS WHY IT CARRIES `rebuild`. /internal-local/ is
      gitignored (.gitignore line 60), so `git clean -fd` cannot reach it and only
      `-fdx` can -- materially safer than the state G109 (e) ruled out of the tree,
      which was untracked AND unignored. It cannot become tracked: PUBLISH-BOUNDARY
      forbids committing credential material, permanently. What makes that
      survivable rather than a standing defect is that THE SYSTEM'S OWN PAYLOAD
      here -- the credential file -- is REBUILDABLE in one command by the operator
      who owns it, where the Confluence capture needed a company-side re-scrape.
      `rebuild:` is scoped to that payload and says nothing about the rest of the
      directory: the deepdoc corpus and the Confluence scripts beside it are the
      operator's, travel by hand, and that command does not bring them back. The
      zone is declared to keep the system OUT, not to promise the directory is
      disposable. G126 declares where the file already is and
      moves nothing -- relocating a machine-local file with no committed source is
      how you destroy the only copy.
      NO `env:` ROW, AND THAT IS A LIMIT WORTH NAMING RATHER THAN HIDING.
      DRYDOCS_CONSOLE_CREDENTIALS names a FILE; a zone's `env:` override resolves
      a DIRECTORY, so wiring the two would make this zone resolve to a file path
      and report "absent" forever. A machine that sets the variable has moved its
      credentials outside this declaration's reach and nothing here can follow
      them -- the same shape as the runtime leg G81 recorded, where a
      caller-supplied path is invisible to any comparison of declarations. What
      IS mechanical is the unset case: a guard asserts credentials_path()
      resolves inside this zone, so the declaration cannot drift from the code
      that owns the path.

surfaces.title: Source bindings (one connection profile per carrier; variable NAMES only)
surfaces.content:
# =============================================================================
# config/source-bindings.yaml — THE BINDING TABLE (G125; ADR 0017, ACCEPTED
# 2026-08-30).
#
# WHAT THIS FILE IS. A registry row says WHAT a source is. This file says HOW to
# REACH the carrier it lives on — and it says it by naming ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES,
# never by holding a value. The registry names the source; a profile names the
# connection; neither holds a host, a service name, a SID or a credential.
#
# WHY IT EXISTS. Fifteen of the thirty dataset rows are `acquisition.mode:
# automated` and declared no binding at all: their system rows carried
# `locator.service: ~` with a comment saying the real value lives in
# `internal-local/`, and nothing resolves a comment. So `drydocs landing-zones
# --check` reported a clean run over the manual half and said nothing about the
# other half — a check that silently covers half its subject reads as coverage.
#
# THE GRAIN (ADR 0017 clause 2 as amended). One profile per CONNECTION CARRIER,
# inherited by every dataset beneath it — NOT per origin. The registry disproves
# per-origin: `origin: controlm` spans three systems, so a per-origin row cannot
# bind to one connection; and `system: psgmgr` carries three origins, so keying
# per origin re-fragments the connection this table exists to share. Four
# carriers cover all fifteen automated datasets.
#
# WHICH ROW POINTS AT WHICH. A system row in config/source-registry.yaml carries
# `binding: <profile id>`, or `binding: ~` with a `binding_note` saying why it has
# none. The reference is GUARDED in both directions (tests/unit/
# test_source_bindings.py): a row naming a profile that does not exist fails, and
# a profile no row names is reported. DataHub ships this same standalone-profile
# shape and omits exactly that link, which is why it is written down here — a
# profile nothing references is a profile nothing can audit.
#
# THE VALUE RULE, and it is a publish-boundary rule (CLAUDE.md §3). Every `env:`
# entry is a bare ${NAME} reference to a variable declared in
# drydocs_core/env_refs.py. Bash-style defaults (${VAR:-x}) are REFUSED, not
# unimplemented: a default in committed YAML puts G81 (d)'s silent relocation back
# at the syntax level where the one expansion function cannot see it. A literal
# value in any of these fields is a test failure.
#
# WHICH TWIN DOCUMENTS IT (G129 (d)). Every profile names the machine-local
# file that holds the coordinates its variables resolve to, or `twin: ~` with the
# reason in its note. The pointer lives HERE rather than in a separate index of
# the machine-local tree, because an index of twenty directories is a second
# surface to keep in step and it rots the first time nobody updates it. The path
# is a POINTER, never a value -- naming a gitignored file is not publishing its
# contents, and it is the whole difference between `locator.service: ~ # lives in
# internal-local/` and a reader who can actually find it.
#
# WHAT A BINDING IS NOT. It is not an instance coordinate and it does not change
# any identifier. ADR 0017 clause 1 defers the instance axis and rules that
# un-redacting `[db]`/`[schema]` must move together with SourceEntry.urn, under
# its own SME gate. Nothing here touches a dataset id or a derived URN.
# =============================================================================
schema: drydocs.source-bindings.v1
updated: 2026-08-30 # G125 — first build, from ADR 0017 (ACCEPTED 2026-08-30)

profiles:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - id: oracle-psgmgr
    twin: internal-local/oracle-connection-consolidated.md   # G129 (d) — which twin documents these coordinates
    carrier: psgmgr
    platform: oracle-db
    classification: Internal
    env:
      user: "${ORACLE_USER}"
      password: "${ORACLE_PASSWORD}"
      dsn: "${ORACLE_DSN}"
    serves: 10 # every automated dataset on this carrier
    note: >
      The Control-M replica. ONE Oracle account reads all ten views, which is
      exactly the situation a NAMED PROFILE suits and a derived
      one-secret-per-source path does not (ADR 0017 clause 4, the Purview shape
      over OpenMetadata's).

      CARRIER-VALUE CAVEAT, recorded rather than silently relied on (ADR 0017
      clause 2 qualification i): `psgmgr` is a SCHEMA, and the database it sits in
      is `spiderdb` — which the registry names nowhere, because it is the token
      `[db]` redacts in all ten ids. So keying this profile on `psgmgr` is a
      proxy that holds only while one schema equals one database. A second schema
      in `spiderdb`, or a `psgmgr` schema in a second database, breaks it
      silently. `spiderdb` is a NAME and publishes (ruled 2026-08-30, the
      pronounceable head of the TNS alias); the rest of the alias and what it
      resolves to stay in the twin, and ORACLE_DSN is where they live.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - id: oracle-drydocs-stg
    twin: internal-local/oracle-connection-consolidated.md   # G129 (d) — which twin documents these coordinates
    carrier: drydocs-stg
    platform: oracle-db
    classification: Internal
    env:
      user: "${ORACLE_USER}"
      password: "${ORACLE_PASSWORD}"
      dsn: "${ORACLE_DSN}"
    serves: 1
    note: >
      The staging schema for the app-fact join. It shares the psgmgr account
      today, which is WHY it is a separate profile rather than a second reference
      to the same one: the profiles are separate declarations that currently
      resolve to the same variables, so the day staging moves behind its own
      account the change is one row here and no id anywhere. Sharing a profile
      would make that a migration.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - id: oracle-inventory
    twin: internal-local/oracle-connection-consolidated.md   # G129 (d) — which twin documents these coordinates
    carrier: oracle
    platform: oracle-db
    classification: Internal
    env:
      user: "${ORACLE_USER}"
      password: "${ORACLE_PASSWORD}"
      dsn: "${ORACLE_DSN}"
    serves: 1
    note: >
      The schema-inventory probe — a catalog read of the instance itself rather
      than of one schema. Same account today; separate profile for the same
      reason as drydocs-stg.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - id: snowflake-catalog
    twin: ~   # G129 (d) — no twin yet; see status below
    carrier: snowflake
    platform: snowflake
    classification: Internal
    env: {} # DELIBERATELY EMPTY — see below
    serves: 3
    status: declared-unconfigured
    note: >
      DECLARED WITH NO VARIABLES YET, and that is a state rather than an omission.
      The three Snowflake datasets are registered and unconfirmed; no Snowflake
      account exists on either machine, so there is nothing for a variable to
      hold. Declaring the profile empty is what makes that VISIBLE — the check
      reports "declared, no variables" instead of the carrier being absent from
      the report altogether, which is the coverage lie this whole item exists to
      end. When an account appears, this grows an `env:` block and nothing else
      changes.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CARRIERS WITH NO BINDING, and the reason each has none. A system absent from
# BOTH lists is a test failure: silence is how "which sources are undeclared"
# became an investigation in the first place. The pattern is data-zones.yaml's —
# its header records why a write zone has no registry row.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
unbound:
  - carrier: airflow
    reason: placeholder vendor — mapped to the BMC baseline, no export feed exists
  - carrier: autosys
    reason: placeholder vendor — mapped to the BMC baseline, no export feed exists
  - carrier: bitbucket
    reason: manual acquisition — the promotion-repo clone lands in a declared drop zone
  - carrier: catalog
    reason: >
      an ORIGIN, not a carrier — its datasets sit on the `snowflake` carrier and
      inherit that profile. Kept here so the absence is declared rather than
      inferred.
  - carrier: controlm
    reason: >
      an ORIGIN, not a carrier — the Control-M XML export is hand-carried into a
      drop zone, and the replica it also feeds is reached through `oracle-psgmgr`.
  - carrier: dpl
    reason: manual acquisition — per-SEAL Swagger exports land in the G19 drop zone
  - carrier: exec-hosts
    reason: manual acquisition — the host inventory is a hand-dropped extract
  - carrier: infra
    reason: manual acquisition — infrastructure notes are hand-maintained
  - carrier: pat
    reason: manual acquisition — the people/product reports are hand-pulled
  - carrier: repo
    reason: the repository itself — read from the working tree, not over a connection
  - carrier: seal
    reason: >
      an ORIGIN, not a carrier — the application extract is hand-dropped, and the
      escalation table it also names is reached through `oracle-psgmgr`.
  - carrier: snow
    reason: >
      manual acquisition TODAY and moving (Idea-132): the ServiceNow extracts are
      hand-pulled CSV becoming SQL over the replica. When that flips, this row
      becomes a profile — which is the transition N12's `acquisition.mode` field
      exists to make visible.

surfaces.title: Log kinds (root, level, retention, rotation, format per kind)
surfaces.content:
# =============================================================================
# config/log-kinds.yaml — every log KIND the system writes, declared with its
# directory, level, retention, rotation and format
# =============================================================================
# G105, ADR 0014 clause 1 AS AMENDED AT THE 2026-08-25 RULING. The clause as
# drafted gave ONE global log_dir / log_level / log_retention_days; the SME ruled
# it per-KIND on a broader principle — "the goal is to have everything
# configurable, not hardcode."
#
# WHY THIS FILE HAD TO EXIST BEFORE ANYTHING COULD BE CONFIGURED PER KIND.
# `kind` was a filename convention, not a code concept. Three sites minted it and
# none agreed:
#   drydocs_core/run_log.py      hardcoded the literal `load.` prefix
#   agents/common/llm_ledger.py  hardcoded `qa.graph_qa`
#   adapters/sql_run_log.py      took a caller-supplied base_name with NO prefix
#                                enforcement, so it wrote `oracle.<ts>.log` and
#                                could have written any kind it liked
# Nothing can be configured per kind while no declaration says what the kinds ARE.
#
# THE NAMING RULE IS DERIVED FROM THIS FILE, NOT ASSERTED BESIDE IT (clause 3 as
# amended). The rule is:
#
#     <kind>.<name>.<stamp>.<ext>
#
# where <stamp> granularity comes from the kind's `rotation` (per-run ->
# YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS, per-day -> YYYYmmdd) and <ext> from its `format`. <name> stays
# FREE-FORM, which is what makes `load.code_snapshot.v1.<ts>.log` conforming — the
# version sits inside <name>, and the drafted rule that spelled the stamp out
# matched only 5 of 86 real files because it did not know that.
#
# The per-day `qa.graph_qa.<YYYYmmdd>.jsonl` ledger is CONFORMING under this rule,
# not excepted: kind=qa, name=graph_qa, stamp=20260820, ext=jsonl. The drafted
# clause called it "the one exception" and flagged itself with "one exception in a
# naming rule is how naming rules die"; deriving the rule removes the exception
# instead of defending it.
#
# ROOT, AND WHY IT IS ONE BLOCK. Every kind hangs off one root, resolved in ONE
# place. config/data-zones.yaml's `run-logs` zone declares `env: DRYDOCS_LOGDIR`
# and data_zones._resolve() ignores the field, so with the variable set that zone
# resolves to the untouched default while every real log lands elsewhere. A single
# root block is the shape in which that class cannot recur. (The zone-resolver bug
# and the guard gap behind it are Idea-171's residue and are NOT fixed here.)
schema: drydocs.log-kinds.v1

root:
  base: home # under the user's home directory, the run-log idiom since G19
  path: logs/DryDocs/
  env: DRYDOCS_LOGDIR
  legacy_env: SPIDERP_LOGDIR # honored ONE more cycle, with a deprecation warning
  note: >
    SCOPE FENCE, carried from G81 (d): unlike DRYDOCS_DATA_ROOT this keeps its
    default and is NOT mandatory. G81 named the DATA root deliberately — a
    relocated log is annoying where a relocated data root is destructive. The
    legacy variable's removal trigger is the next port after ADR 0014 was
    accepted; "one cycle" with no event attached is how a deprecation becomes
    permanent.

defaults:
  level: INFO
  retention_days: 90
  rotation: per-run # per-run -> <YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS> | per-day -> <YYYYmmdd>
  format: log # log | jsonl
  dir: ~ # null = the root itself; a kind may name a subdirectory

kinds:
  - id: load
    writer: drydocs_core.run_log.LoaderRunLog
    note: >
      84 of the 86 files in the directory today. `name` is the loader id and
      already carries its own version segment (code_snapshot.v1) — which is why
      <name> is free-form in the derived rule rather than a bare identifier.

  - id: sql
    writer: drydocs_core.adapters.sql_run_log.SqlRunLog
    note: >
      The family that could write ANY kind: SqlRunLog(self.name) from
      oracle_adapter, so it wrote `oracle.<ts>.log` with no kind segment at all.
      Declaring it is what makes that checkable. It shares run_log's directory
      resolver already (it imports claim_log_path) — the two families never
      disagreed about WHERE, only about the filename.

  - id: cli
    writer: drydocs.cli.configure_logging
    rotation: per-day
    note: >
      The dictConfig FILE SINK — the general console stream teed to disk, not a
      run artifact, which is why it rotates per day like the ledger rather than
      per invocation. Declared because the sink was first written as
      `drydocs.cli.log`, a name that quietly did not conform to the very rule
      this file derives: `drydocs` is not a kind. A sink exempt from the naming
      rule it ships alongside is how the rule stops meaning anything.

  - id: qa
    writer: agents.common.llm_ledger
    rotation: per-day
    format: jsonl
    note: >
      Append-only ledger, not a run artifact — per-run files would shard one
      queryable history, and its `run` line is the ONLY place the full question
      text lands (:AgentRun carries sha256 + length). Retention is the shared 90
      days by SME ruling rather than an exemption: 90 days of question text is
      what makes the ledger useful for search metrics, where an unbounded ledger
      is an audit relic. The consequence is deliberate and stated — sweeping it
      destroys the only record that turns a hash back into words.

  - id: api
    writer: drydocs_api.audit.ApiAuditLog
    rotation: per-day
    format: jsonl
    note: >
      One audit line per drydocs_api route that executes Cypher OR WRITES —
      widened from Cypher-only at the ruling, because intake.py writes to the data
      root and would otherwise be the one filesystem-touching surface with no
      trail. Lean by design: no Cypher text, no result values, actor hashed
      (sha256, the :AgentRun function). 90 days because the purpose is a metrics
      window on what is searched. The writer's docstring carries the audited-route
      enumeration (G108); the correlation_id field joins these lines to the qa
      ledger's run_id.

  - id: api-debug
    writer: drydocs_api.audit.ApiAuditLog
    retention_days: 7
    format: jsonl
    note: >
      The trace/debug tier, ruled a SEPARATE KIND rather than `api` at DEBUG
      level so a 90-day metrics record is never buried in debug noise and debug
      can be deleted aggressively without touching the audit. It DOES carry
      Cypher text and request detail; Cypher is bounded at 20,000 chars with a
      cypher_truncated flag (audit.CYPHER_TEXT_BOUND — the stated size bound).
      OFF UNLESS THIS DECLARATION SAYS level: DEBUG — verbose is settings-level,
      not per-request: an HTTP request has no --verbose, and a per-request header
      would let an untrusted caller enable verbose capture of their own traffic.
      HELD FOR SME REVIEW: whether this text is ever DISPLAYED in the console.
      Capturing it is ruled; surfacing it is not.

  - id: search
    writer: drydocs_deepdoc.search_log.SearchLog
    rotation: per-day
    format: jsonl
    note: >
      MM3 — the deepdoc search log: one line per connector search (tool, search,
      theme = the mind-map slot targeted, novelty + the new ids, results, date,
      seed). The three session search scripts kept this as a shared CSV under
      DRYDOCS_LOGDIR; it joins the family here as a declared kind. Append-only
      per-day ledger like `qa`, and for the same reason: novelty is "new ids vs
      the graph + the record", and the record IS this file — a per-run file
      would shard the one history the score reads. A row with no theme is
      refused before any I/O (drydocs_deepdoc.search_log). Retention is the
      shared 90 days; the map the rows target is the durable record, the log is
      how it got filled.

surfaces.title: Dev/test environment names
surfaces.content:
# =============================================================================
# config/dev-environment.yaml — canonical local dev/test infrastructure names
# =============================================================================
# Single source of truth for the names and ports the local dev/test stack uses.
# The .env.example templates (root, agents/, web/) and the run-drydocs skill all
# defer to this file — when the container or ports change, change them HERE and
# refresh the templates, not the other way around.
#
# Contains NO company data and NO secrets (names/ports only; passwords live in
# gitignored .env files, never in a committed file).
schema: drydocs.dev-environment.v1

neo4j:
  # Local Neo4j Enterprise container (EE required — ADR 0002 multi-DB + composite;
  # Aura ruled out 2026-07-06). Provision the topology once after first start:
  # drydocs_core/schema/provisioning/provision.ps1
  container: neo4jtest
  image: neo4j:2026.05.0-enterprise   # store written by 2026.05.0 — cannot downgrade to 5.26
  volume: neo4j-testdata              # -> /data   (the graph; survives container recreation)
  plugins_volume: neo4j-testplugins   # -> /plugins (see `plugins:` below)
  plugins: [apoc, graph-data-science]
  # PLUGINS ARE A MOUNTED VOLUME, NOT `NEO4J_PLUGINS` (fixed 2026-07-28). The env-var
  # form asks the entrypoint to DOWNLOAD each plugin at startup; when that download
  # cannot happen the container starts anyway and the plugin is simply absent — which
  # is exactly what was found: `NEO4J_PLUGINS=[apoc]` was set for weeks while
  # /plugins held only README.txt, so `drydocs bootstrap` refused with "APOC required"
  # and the neo4j-drydocs MCP server could not work. Both jars SHIP INSIDE the image
  # (/var/lib/neo4j/labs for apoc, /var/lib/neo4j/products for GDS) and are version-
  # matched to the server, so populating a named volume from the image needs no network
  # and cannot drift from the server version. Populate + create: see the header of
  # drydocs_core/schema/provisioning/provision.ps1 (guarded by tests/unit/test_dev_environment.py).
  # Requires the procedure allowlists — apoc.*,gds.* in BOTH unrestricted and allowlist.
  ports:
    http: 7474            # browser UI  -> http://localhost:7474
    bolt: 7687            # drivers     -> bolt://localhost:7687
  # Docker can remap host ports (an earlier container, neo4j-drydocs-ee, landed on
  # 7476/7689 — retired 2026-07-23: data migrated into the neo4j-testdata volume and
  # this canonical container recreated on 7474/7687; the old container is kept stopped
  # (restart=no) as a rollback copy). If a connection is refused, trust
  # `docker port <container>` over any template value.
  databases:              # ADR 0002 topology — provisioned, not implicit
    # (a `lineage: ddlineage` row lived here until 2026-08-04 — retired, ADR 0002 X1
    # amendment; curated lineage writes land in ground_truth per D1/D2)
    ground_truth: drydocs      # main load + lineage writers; default load target;
                               # ALSO the uncertain realm since G102 (2026-08-18):
                               # gate document-content-topology folded the content
                               # topology to one database — uncertain writes carry
                               # :Uncertain (deepdoc + agent telemetry, the ruled
                               # allowlist) and every ground-truth QuerySpec
                               # excludes the label structurally.
    # uncertain_context: ddcontext — RETIRED at G102 (was: SYNTHESIZED-only,
    #   drydocs_deepdoc). Existing per-machine databases left inert.
    # composite: ddall — RETIRED at G102: a composite over one database
    #   federates nothing.
    # Schema meta-graph (`drydocs bootstrap-schema-graph`, C21/G51). Its own database
    # because exemplar nodes carry REAL labels beside :SchemaMeta and `drydocs`' NODE
    # KEYs enforce property existence the exemplars don't have. Deliberately NOT an
    # `ddall` constituent: it describes the schema, not the estate, so federating it
    # would present labels as data.
    schema_meta: ddschema
  home_db_warning: >
    The EE home database `neo4j` is NOT part of the topology — loading into it
    puts data where no query surface looks. Set NEO4J_DATABASE to a topology
    database (normally `drydocs`).

services:
  # Local dev servers the web UI expects (see web/.env.example).
  adk_api: 8000           # agents ADK server (VITE_ADK_URL)
  drydocs_api: 8001       # thin read API, ADR 0005 (VITE_API_URL)

data:
  # WHERE SOURCE PAYLOADS AND OUTPUTS LIVE. Every drop zone and every output the
  # system writes is rooted here, which is why G81 (2026-08-23) made it MANDATORY:
  # `resolve_data_root()` RAISES when DRYDOCS_DATA_ROOT is unset or empty rather
  # than falling back. The old fallback (~/data/DryDocs) meant the same command in
  # two shells targeted two different trees, so a write meant for one could land on
  # the other and report success either way — the mechanism behind the 2026-08-11
  # overwrite of an SME source folder (docs/reviews/g81-data-path-reconstruction.md).
  #
  # The value is PER MACHINE and never committed: it is a real local path, and this
  # file carries names and ports only. Set it in your shell profile.
  root_env: DRYDOCS_DATA_ROOT
  conventional_location: "~/data/DryDocs"   # what to point it at, not a default
  # What lives under it, with each zone's MODE, is config/data-zones.yaml (write /
  # scratch) plus config/source-registry.yaml `acquisition.drop_dir` (read). The
  # invariant across both: no write path may equal, contain or be contained by a
  # read path (tests/unit/test_data_zones.py).
  zones_declaration: config/data-zones.yaml
  # Run logs keep their default ON PURPOSE (G81 scope fence): a relocated log is
  # annoying, a relocated data root is destructive.
  log_env: DRYDOCS_LOGDIR
  log_default: "~/logs/DryDocs"

shell:
  # RUNTIME text encoding on Windows, per machine, never committed. .editorconfig
  # settles what the FILES are (utf-8, lf) and the guards read files with an
  # explicit encoding, so the tree is fine; what .editorconfig cannot reach is the
  # interpreter's stdout, which on a Windows console defaults to the ANSI code page
  # and dies on the first non-ASCII character a renderer or a test prints (the
  # 2026-09-02 symptom: a pipeline that stopped mid-output with no error - J76's
  # class). Set BOTH in the user environment, the same way DRYDOCS_DATA_ROOT is set:
  #   PYTHONUTF8=1          - the interpreter runs in UTF-8 mode (files AND streams)
  #   PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 - the streams alone; covers an interpreter that ignores
  #                            the first (an embedded or older one)
  # A Claude Code shell does not inherit them reliably, so `export PYTHONIOENCODING=
  # utf-8` at the head of the command is the working habit there.
  utf8_env: [PYTHONUTF8, PYTHONIOENCODING]

depgraph:
  # The code-graph INSTRUMENT (U7). knowledge/depgraph-snapshots/snapshot.ps1
  # shells out to this sibling checkout, so the revision here decides what a
  # snapshot can see — it is dev infrastructure exactly like the container above.
  repo: ../depgraph       # sibling of the DryDocs repo root, NOT a submodule
  remote: https://github.com/ce-wilson/depgraph.git
  # FORK CONSOLIDATED 2026-07-28 (depgraph 5006567). It was two divergent
  # siblings off a one-commit main — feat/p0-vector (--tree) and
  # feat/controlm-lineage (the U6 multi-root resolver) — with neither an
  # ancestor of the other, so no revision had everything and a plain clone of
  # `main` reproduced the broken scanner. Both are now merged into main and the
  # branches are DELETED (local + remote); main is the only branch. Track main.
  #
  # PIN BUMPED 2026-08-04: 5006567 -> 773fb1e, on the SAME main and a clean
  # descendant of the old pin — 9c663ca (RUA inventory ingestion + a shallow
  # script-op analyzer) then the 773fb1e merge, which unions REL_TYPES with
  # TRANSFERS / RUNS_ON / CONTAINS. Found at a session close: the LAPTOP sibling
  # was still on 5006567 while the DESKTOP had already written that day's
  # snapshot with 773fb1e, so the two machines were measuring with different
  # instruments — which by itself defeats the drift comparison the snapshots
  # exist for. The pin had also simply gone stale: it named a revision main had
  # moved past.
  # MEASURED, because the first reading of this was WRONG and the correction is
  # the useful part: the stale revision would NOT have undercounted this repo.
  # Scanning DryDocs emits exactly one relationship type — CONTAINS (1772) —
  # with TRANSFERS and RUNS_ON at zero in both the desktop's snapshot and the
  # post-bump one, and an identical 526 edges. Those two types come from
  # depgraph's Control-M / RUA lineage extractors, which a Python-tree scan of
  # this repo never exercises. So "newer instrument" was worth having for
  # comparability and currency, not because output was being lost here. Treat a
  # REL_TYPES change as a reason to re-measure, not as proof of an undercount.
  # Verified after the bump (laptop; probe run the way snapshot.ps1 runs it,
  # PYTHONPATH=. inside the sibling): importable, multi_root and tree all true.
  # Note WHY the probe below could not have caught the drift: both revisions
  # pass it, because the new commits add edge TYPES rather than a capability.
  # The pin is therefore the only check on instrument currency, and keeping it
  # current is a maintenance obligation, not a formality. STALE CLAUSE STRUCK
  # 2026-08-11: this used to end "nothing yet compares the checkout against this
  # value automatically — that gap is in IDEAS.md". It was closed the same
  # session it was raised — snapshot.ps1 reads `expected_commit` here and warns
  # on ahead/behind/unknown (and it fired correctly tonight on an unfetched
  # pin). Left as a struck note rather than deleted because the sentence had
  # already misled a reader into believing the drift was unwatched.
  expected_branch: main
  # PIN BUMPED 2026-08-09 (U19): a56d2fc -> 6ee0af6, same main, clean
  # descendant. The extractor now resolves bare-name imports against the
  # FILE's own sys.path root — the directory Python itself would put on the
  # path (walk up while __init__.py is present; the first ancestor that is
  # not a package is the root). Before it, `scripts/render_board.py` doing
  # `import render_gates` and `agents/graph_qa/*` doing `from common import`
  # resolved to nothing, so both regions recorded ZERO internal edges and
  # read as orphans in every metric that counts them.
  # THIS IS AN INSTRUMENT CHANGE, so the edge count jumps for that reason and
  # not because the repo grew — the same rule as the O42 and U6 bumps. The
  # change is additive by construction (the extra root is appended after the
  # project roots, pinned by a test), so no edge that already resolved moves.
  # Pushed to origin before the bump, so the laptop can reach the revision
  # this file now names; a pin naming an unpushed commit is the 2026-08-04
  # two-machine divergence with extra steps.
  # PIN BUMPED 2026-08-06 (O42): a56d2fc adds the ts-imports extractor —
  # first-party .ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx edges in every plain scan. Edge-count
  # jump across this bump is the instrument, not growth (snapshots README).
  expected_commit: 6ee0af6
  # What snapshot.ps1 REFUSES to scan without. These are probed behaviourally
  # (knowledge/depgraph-snapshots/probe_instrument.py) rather than by version
  # string — capability is the thing that matters, and depgraph's 0.1.0 spans
  # both the broken and the fixed resolver, so a version says nothing.
  requires:
    scan: [multi_root]    # every run
    tree: [tree]          # additionally, when -Tree is passed
  # Does the live-capability test ASSERT against the checkout, or skip?
  # True producer-side: the sibling is ours, a missing capability is a real defect
  # here, and failing loudly is the entire point of U7. A consumer whose depgraph
  # fork is separately owned — and so cannot be remediated by a port — sets this
  # FALSE with the owed action recorded, and flips it back when the fork catches up
  # (PORT-REPORT-94132c80 / owed action 48e). Deliberately a config flag and NOT an
  # env var or a second test variant: this file is canonical-company in
  # PORT-MANIFEST.yaml, so the divergence lives in the one file already ruled
  # per-side and tests/unit/test_probe_instrument.py stays BYTE-IDENTICAL on both
  # sides — nothing to reconcile at the next port.
  capability_assert: true
